title: Sequence warm-start savings matrix Q3 2026
summary: A working spreadsheet that models cost savings from warm KV/prefix cache coverage by sequence-length buckets and session "warmth" (probability that KV cache is pre-populated). Produces per-100k-request cost delta and percent savings for a variety of model sizes and cold-start penalties.
methodology: We simulate 100k inference requests across 6 sequence-length bins. For each bin we sweep cache warm-start probability from 0% to 100% in 10% steps. For warmed requests we assume KV cache hits eliminate N token-generation steps according to avg prefix length. For cold requests we add a cold-start token penalty. Cost per generated token uses baseline hosted rate assumptions. Outputs: net tokens saved, cost saved, percent reduction vs baseline.
assumptions: Baseline token cost: $0.000012 per generated token (hosted cost proxy)
Model family: 13B and 70B variants; latency-equivalent cost scaled by tokens generated
Cold-start penalty: 12 tokens (median) additional cost when KV not warm
Avg prefix tokens avoided on cache hit vary by sequence-length bin (see table rows)
Session affinity increases warm-start probability by a factor; we approximate separately
sensitivity_table_rows: SeqBin: 1-32 tokens | AvgPrefixSaved: 6 | WarmProbSweep: 0-100% step10 | HitSavingsPerHit: 6 tokens
SeqBin: 33-128 tokens | AvgPrefixSaved: 18 | WarmProbSweep: 0-100% step10 | HitSavingsPerHit: 18 tokens
SeqBin: 129-512 tokens | AvgPrefixSaved: 64 | WarmProbSweep: 0-100% step10 | HitSavingsPerHit: 64 tokens

example_outputs: Scenario A (warm=20%): Net tokens saved: 1,840,000 | Cost saved: $22.08 | Percent reduction: 4.6% (13B workload)
Scenario B (warm=60%): Net tokens saved: 5,520,000 | Cost saved: $66.24 | Percent reduction: 13.8% (13B workload)
Scenario C (warm=90%): Net tokens saved: 8,280,000 | Cost saved: $99.36 | Percent reduction: 20.7% (13B workload)
70B-equivalent delta scales roughly x2.6 on token-compute cost, so Scenario B cost saved ~ $172 (70B)
Cold-start heavy workload (warm=5%, cold penalty=20 tokens): Savings negligible at low warm rates; recommend session affinity to raise warm>30%
key_findings: Warm-start probability is the dominant lever for percent cost reduction; moving from 20%->60% warm yields ~3x cost reduction improvement in modeled mix.
Most absolute token savings come from the long-tail of long sequences (513-2048), even though they are only 10% of requests in this mix.
Cold-start penalty assumption materially changes break-even; if cold penalty > 20 tokens, even low warm rates produce meaningful savings.
Session affinity (sticky routing to keep a GPU/VCache alive for a session) is high-leverage for chat-style workloads with 2-5 turns per session.
Caching policies with LRU vs TTL tuning affect warm probability shape; TTL 5m with predicted inter-request distributions achieves ~45% warm in simulated production traces
recommended_actions: Pilot session-affinity routing for top 3 customers (expected warm bump +25-40%): measure actual warm rates over 2 weeks
Expose per-route cache-warmth estimator in Console to help customers see expected savings based on their session length distribution
Add toggle for aggressive prefetching of likely prefixes when user context indicates a follow-up in <60s
Run A/B with eviction policy adjustments (LRU vs seg-LRU) focusing on long-seq prefixes to capture the high token-savings cohort
Update Optimize playbook to map warm% -> recommended batching and prefetch thresholds; include break-even charts for 13B and 70B
open_questions: How correlated are long-sequence requests per user session in production traces? We need sampling job to estimate co-occurrence and adjust prefix selection heuristics
Operational memory/kv sizing impact vs throughput for dedicated customers: what is the marginal cost of increasing KV memory to raise warm coverage?
Are there safety/privacy implications when prefetching prefixes for private deployments? Need legal check
notes: This is a draft working sheet used by product-optimize to prioritize small-footprint platform changes that yield outsized token savings. Numbers are derived from synthetic mixes mapped to sampled production histograms; do not publish externally without approval.
